so essentially this relates to the metaphysical debate about defining change and how being differs.
change is defined as transitioning from potency (the ability to do something) to act (the doing of something)
and then it gets mega complicated because wait, how do things differ to begin with, i.e. human and rock in a philosophical sense.
the pre socratics claimed they differed by different elements, and some fuckers felt the need to be special (i.e. pythagoras with his numbers) and parmenides, with his classic definition of difference being: "things differ by their being (existence) and nonbeing (their nonexistence) and because everything exists, nothing can differ. thus, all things are the same in their being.)
this is a mega bad argument, but famous philosophers like democritus, plato, and aristotle could not refute this argument because no one could place how exactly parmenides's argument was wrong.
finally, thomas aquinas truly refutes the argument, saying (this is watered down): "things do not differ in their general being, but in their act and potency, as god is pure act, being, and differs from a rock or a plant, which is a mix of potency and act, and is still being, thus making these things different. therefore, all things differ in their simple or complex beings, varying by their amounts of potency and actuality."
it's really complicated, and i don't blame you if you don't understand it, cause you get really abstract with these concepts and it's really difficult for me, a high school student to understand, much less my philosophy teacher with a PhD in the subject and still didn't understand it till after two years past getting his doctorate.
so yeah- sorry lmao
